narrative.overview: A security console is used mid-task, for hours, by someone deciding whether to trust a machine. The system behaves like a well-made instrument: a quiet neutral ground, white cards with hairline edges, one warm accent spent on action and on the data line, and figures set in a monospaced face so columns of numbers read as measurements. It is modelled on the pinned reference dashboard and translated to alert triage. Depth is tonal; nothing glows except the brand mark and the chart line. The dark theme is the same token set re-pointed.
keyCharacteristics: Top navigation; content on a neutral ground; a 340px right rail on the dashboard.
One accent (Ember) for primary actions, active state, brand mark and the data line.
Every figure in Geist Mono with tabular numerals; every status has a text label.
Explanation is visible at rest: a SHAP mini-profile in every alert row, a resting crosshair on every chart.
Synthetic provenance is always labelled, never hidden.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Ember appears on one primary action per region and on the data line.

rules.name: The Label Rule
rules.body: Colour never carries meaning alone; severity, status and deltas always include text or an arrow.

rules.name: The Dark Ramp Rule
rules.body: In dark theme, ordinal ramps are re-derived from Ember at rising lightness so their order survives.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Anything that is a measured quantity is Geist Mono with tabular numerals; anything that is a word is Geist.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Floating Rule
rules.body: Only overlays cast a real shadow.

dos: Do keep primary text on Ember as Ink (#18181c); if white is ever wanted, use a darker accent, not white on #ff7646.
Do set every measured value in Geist Mono with tabular numerals.
Do pair every status colour with its word (Critical, Confirmed, Demo data).
Do label generated data wherever it could be mistaken for live traffic: "Synthetic data", "Demo data", "Simulated".
Do derive dark-theme ramps from the accent at rising lightness.
donts: Don't use a sidebar, a crimson brand colour, or neon-on-black "cyber" styling.
Don't add eyebrows or kickers above headings, gradient text, coloured side-stripes on cards, or hard offset shadows.
Don't use sparklines or micro-charts as decoration; every micro-visual must encode real data.
Don't animate layout properties; motion is state change only, and reduced-motion is honoured.
Don't let a table or chart widen the page; contain overflow inside its card.
